links.note: '1857 ki top' points to the first war of independence; 25099 is the concept that names the 1857 top placed at the Company Bagh muhana
'dhar rakhi gayi hai' means kept as a dharohar -- 25105 glosses virasat as things received from earlier generations
which war this top served in -> India's first freedom struggle, the 1857 dating that 25099 carries
when in the year the top is polished -> Independence and Republic Day; 25100 is the twice-a-year polishing
what the top tells the sailani about itself -> that it was powerful and made of steel; 25101 is its boast about blowing apart surmas
how the top is looked after -> like the inherited Company Bagh; 25100 says the top too gets great sambhaal
gloss of 'baharhaal', the word that opens the line 'ab to baharhaal chhote ladkon ki ghudsawari se' -- concept 25102
gloss of 'faarig' (free, empty) in 'agar yah faarig ho', the same ghudsawari clause, so 25102
what the chidiyan do sitting on the top -> gapshap, 25103 word for word
what the gauraiya does in mischief -- 25103 is the sparrow going right inside; the marked option here says it tampers with the parts, which the poem does not say, but the concept is the same
gloss of 'muhane' = entrance; the phrase belongs to 25099, the top at the Company Bagh muhana
what we received in virasat -> the top; 25105 is the virasat gloss
how the top is cared for -> polished twice a year, 25100 exactly
whose dhajje the top blew apart -- 25101 is that boast (this row's stem is damaged, another lesson's text running into it, but the leading stem is intact)
why inherited things are so carefully kept -> they carry us back to our past and ancestors, which is 25096, the dharohar that gives us the bhaan of ancient attainments; 25105 is only the word-gloss
what the poem tells us about the top -- an omnibus recall answered from its identity as the 1857 gun standing in Company Bagh, 25099
the lesson the top gives -> however strong, one must fall silent one day; 25104 is the mouth-must-close concept
the two occasions for polishing -> 15 August and 26 January, the twice-a-year of 25100
the bhaav of the 'chhote ladkon ki ghudsawari' lines -- 25102, the children riding it
the bhaav of 'kitni bhi badi ho top ek din to hona hi hai uska munh band' -- 25104 verbatim
'uda diye the maine achchhe-achchhe surmaon ke dhajje' -- that line IS 25101
what the poet means by 'achchhe-achchhe surmaon ke dhajje' -> the revolutionaries it killed; 25101, not 25106 which is only the word-gloss of dhajje
what the poem tells us about the top, asked again -> its identity as the 1857 gun in Company Bagh, 25099
bhaav of the munh-band lines -- 25104
the sandesh of the top -> never misuse power because it must one day be powerless; 25104
why the 1857 top is polished twice a year -- 25100
prove that inherited things are carefully kept -- 25096, heritage as the priceless record of our forebears
the same virasat-sambhaal question; its answer field is damaged down to '(gha) anupras' but the stem stands, so 25096
when the sailani come to Company Bagh -> morning and evening, part of the Company-Bagh setting of 25099
why the top is set at the Bagh's muhana -> so visitors remember the patriots martyred in 1857; 25097 is the dharohar that recalls the daman, not 25096 which recalls attainments
gloss of 'jabar' = powerful, the top's own word in its boast, 25101
what the chidiya sit on to gossip -> the top; 25103
what the top is used for now -> the small boys' ghudsawari, 25102
what boys in the Bagh do on the top -> ride it, 25102
which war it served in, asked again -> 1857, so 25099
meaning of virasat -> wealth and things received from forebears; 25105's gloss word for word
the two things received in virasat -> Company Bagh and the top; 25105 is the virasat concept, whereas 25096 is about two KINDS of dharohar, not two objects
why the English built Company Baghs -> for their own strolling; 25098 is the Company arriving and becoming ruler
prose rendering of the poem, whose answer turns on not forgetting the martyrs' sacrifice -- 25097, the dharohar that reminds us of the daman
what the sparrows and birds tell us -> one day the biggest top's mouth closes; 25104
whose oppression the top recounts -> Indians'; 25097 is the daman-remembering dharohar
the lesson of the top -> awareness of the forebears' mistakes and not repeating them, which is 25097's 'poorvajon ki chook'

what the 1857 top does now -> serves as a toy and a memorial; 25102, the children's riding
who gets inside the top -> the birds; 25103
the hallmark of Dangwal's poetry -> the depiction of society's ordinary people, 25094 exactly
which poem the munh-band line comes from -- the line itself is 25104
who wrote 'Top' -> Viren Dangwal; 25093 is the poet's birth-and-education concept
why it stands at the gate -> so nobody forgets that a company like East India must not come again; 25098 is the Company's arrival and takeover

what the top says about itself -> that it was very powerful in its day; 25101

the poet's message -> do not repeat the past's mistakes; 25097 is the 'chook' concept
the birds' message -> every powerful man's mouth closes like the top's; 25104
who comes to Company Bagh morning and evening -> sailani; part of 25099's setting
the lesson of the top, asked again -> the forebears' mistakes and not repeating them; 25097
how problems can be solved according to the poet -> by talking, because the gun is no final answer; that is 25104's point
why the British army used the top -> to crush Indian patriots; 'daman' is 25097's own word
what the top reminds us of -> the freedom struggle; 25097 is the remembering-the-daman dharohar
